01 · Decision view

Mission fit and flight-worthiness

Headline values come from the optimized aircraft’s own artifacts. Every gate below carries one-line evidence and a source path; the green state is not inferred from a stage’s top-level flag alone.

Ready for wider review

The concept meets the encoded mission and all current preliminary-design gates. This is a traceable conceptual design verdict—not an airworthiness certification.

Concept source: designs/ntnu-x8/design.yaml · Optimized spec: results/ntnu-x8/optimized/design.yaml

NTNU May-2023 Skywalker X8 reproduction translated from the source-cited design-time input pack without validation maneuvers or published aerodynamic coefficients. The equivalent trapezoid, NACA 0012 section, washout, molded body, fin attachment, packaging, structure, and drag are declared conceptual abstractions. The motor/controller package is modeled inside the aft body; the external pusher disk is represented by the published thrust deck. The measured 3.364 kg flight mass includes propulsion and battery. Liquid fuel, battery energy, range, and endurance are not claimed. Fuselage fineness, bay dimensions, component packaging, fin attachment, structural properties, mission screens, and solver settings are engineering assumptions checked by the canonical internal gates, not source or validation claims.

03 · Design evolution

From source or sketch to delivered design

The baseline is the aircraft as drawn; the optimizer answers what it presented. Both columns below are read from their own phase artifacts — the two phases are different aircraft and are never mixed inside one number. The delivered configuration is checked by a separate OAS solve; stability evidence is labeled by method.

Baseline phase evidence

What the baseline presented

  • Static margin 0.080 MAC sits inside the 0.03–0.10 design band (measured NP 0.464 m).
  • Pitch trim closes with wing twist at -2.00°.
  • Stall 8.5 m/s against the 12 m/s requirement, from effective CLmax 1.00.
  • Thrust-limited dash 37.4 m/s (M 0.11 vs cap 0.11).
  • Wingbox at ±limit load: +g KS -0.96, −g KS -0.96 (negative values are margin).

Methodology: AERO QA workflow · MDO · OAS · OpenVSP

Assumptions and limitations

  • The electric deck supplies sourced steady thrust only. Battery energy, range, and endurance are outside this reproduction.
  • Stall speed uses CLmax = 1.00; nonlinear separation and high-lift devices are not modeled.
  • OAS and VSPAERO are lifting-surface methods. The fins affect mass, drag, and Vv but do not enter the wing-only OAS stability solve.
  • SU2 is a coarse 2-D Euler section calculation. A successful process return is not aerodynamic convergence.
  • TACS and OAS use different structural idealizations; their discrepancy is calibration information, not interchangeable proof.
  • No propulsion installation loss, inlet distortion, controls, flutter, thermal, landing, manufacturing, or certification analysis is claimed.
